Serve static files over HTTP

Source: R/serve.R
pz_serve_static.Rd

Serves a directory or a single HTML file on a free local port. For a file, its directory is served and the handle URL points to that file. Other files in that directory are also accessible over HTTP.

Usage

pz_serve_static(path, ..., root = NULL)

Arguments

path

A path to a directory or an .html file.

...

Reserved; must be empty.

root

The directory to serve as the server root. Defaults to the file's directory for an .html file. Only supported when path is a file, which must live inside root (both are resolved with normalizePath(), so symlinks are resolved first, and root can't be the filesystem root); the handle URL points at path relative to root. Use it when the page references assets outside its own directory, such as ../deps/styles.css.

Value

A PaparazziServe handle with $url, $port, $stop(), $is_running(), and $logs(). Static servers have no captured logs: $logs() returns character(). Pass the handle to pz_open() to share a server across pages. Closing those pages leaves it running. $stop() is idempotent; use withr::defer(server$stop()) for cleanup. A finalizer stops the server as a last resort.

Examples

# pz_open() serves HTML files over HTTP on its own; pz_serve_static()
# creates a handle you can share across pages instead
server <- pz_serve_static(pz_example("tasks"))
page <- pz_open(server)
pz_get_url(page)
#> [1] "http://127.0.0.1:5953/tasks.html"
pz_close(page)
server$stop()
